en.title: Contrast and concession
en.summary: Contrast shows a difference; concession admits one thing and states another.

paragraphs: Contrast shows how two things differ. Concession admits that one fact is true, but says that the main fact is true in spite of it. English has many linking words for both, and they differ in grammar and formality.

items: **Although** it was cold, we went out.
She is rich; **however**, she is not happy.
Tom likes tea, **whereas** Ann prefers coffee.

blocks.html:
WordFollowed byExample
although / though / even thougha clauseAlthough it rained, we went.
despite / in spite ofa noun or -ingDespite the rain, we went.
whereas / whilea clause (contrast)Tom is tall, whereas Ann is short.
buta clause (between clauses)It is cheap, but it is good.
howevera new sentence, with a commaIt was cheap. However, it was bad.
neverthelessformal, between sentencesIt rained; nevertheless, we went.
yeta clause, after a commaIt is old, yet it works.

paragraphs: Although and despite introduce a dependent concession; they cannot be used together with but in the same sentence. Despite and in spite of take a noun or -ing form, not a clause. With a clause, add the fact that: despite the fact that.

blocks.html:
With a clauseWith a noun or -ing
Although he was ill, he worked.Despite his illness, he worked.
Although it rained, we went.In spite of the rain, we went.
He worked, but he was ill.Despite being ill, he worked.

items: Wrong: **Although it was cold, but we went.** Right: **Although it was cold, we went.**
Wrong: **Despite it was cold,...** Right: **Despite the cold,...** or **Although it was cold,...**
Wrong: **In spite of he was ill,...** Right: **In spite of being ill,...**
Wrong: **However, it is cheap, but good.** Use one connector only.

ro.title: Contrast și concesie
ro.summary: Folosim conectori de contrast și concesie pentru a arăta diferențe sau situații neașteptate între două idei.

paragraphs: Contrastul arată o diferență între două lucruri. Concesia arată o acțiune neașteptată sau o opoziție. Pentru a lega aceste idei, folosim cuvinte de legătură specifice.

items: Eu beau ceai, **dar** el preferă cafeaua.
**Deși** plouă afară, noi mergem la plimbare.
Este frig, **totuși** Maria nu are geacă.

paragraphs: Cuvintele „dar” și „însă” exprimă un contrast direct. După conjuncția „deși” folosim verbul la modul indicativ. Nu folosim niciodată „deși” și „dar” în aceeași frază. De obicei, punem virgulă înaintea acestor conectori.

blocks.html:
ConectorSensExemplu
dar / însăcontrast directVreau să vin, **dar** nu am timp.
deși / cu toate căconcesie cu o propoziție**Deși** este obosit, el lucrează.
totușirezultat opusA învățat mult, **totuși** are emoții.
în ciuda (+ genitiv)concesie cu un substantivAm plecat **în ciuda** vremii rele.
